solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 12 across to 13); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alec stands waving something on the beach

indicators.note: waving suggests the letters of the two words before it flap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Alec stands on the sand waving at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving' rearranges the letters of ALEC STANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's sculpted heap of sand by the sea is a typical thing found at the seaside.

clue.text: Article completes the undoing of relatives

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
to finish undoing a knot or bow is to untie it, so this phrase gives UNTIES

explanation.surface: A grammatical article seems to finish off the undoing of family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters of one's parents are family members, so the plural is a fair synonym for relatives.

clue.text: Party, alternatively, providing means of escape?

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone at a party is looking for a way out, or something like it.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit through a hinged panel in a wall is a way to get out of a room, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Primate's name secretary recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters are turned round to run in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A secretary remembers the name of a primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NAMEPA end to end. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape-like early human or hominid is a kind of primate.

clue.text: Be visibly embarrassed after little boy beamed?

indicators.note: after places BE RED behind the boy's name

parts.note: Tim is a short boy's name, from Timothy
taken as written
someone visibly embarrassed has gone red

explanation.surface: A small boy grins but then blushes with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beamed' looks like 'smiled', but it means fitted with wooden beams.
explanation.definitionFit: A building fitted with wooden beams is made with timber, a cryptic reading of beamed.

clue.text: Nobleman years ahead of his time

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: An aristocrat was a man years ahead of his era.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving before the expected hour means being ahead of time, a synonym for premature.

clue.text: Maybe Chinese food at the back

parts.note: fare is food served
astern is the nautical word for towards the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Perhaps Chinese takeaway food is kept round the back.
explanation.definitionFit: China lies in eastern Asia, so Chinese is an example of something from that region.

clue.text: Offer comfort to Tory only

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: Someone is told to reassure only the Conservative party member.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone in grief is to comfort them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Protective material, designed to cool, won't

indicators.note: designed implies the letters are arranged into a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: A protective fabric designed to keep you cool turns out not to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges TO COOL WONT, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy raw cotton fibres are used to pad and protect fragile things, giving a protective material.

clue.text: Some backing from fair American girl

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some support comes from a fair-minded American girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes AIRAM from inside 'fair American' and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a common female first name, so it serves as a girl.

clue.text: Jolly experience with LSD

definitions.meaning: a jolly is an outing or excursion
a hallucinogenic drug episode is called by the same word

explanation.surface: A cheerful experience involving the drug LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an outing and a drug-induced hallucinatory episode share this one short word.

clue.text: Rudely jeer any English novel

indicators.note: rudely suggests the letters are roughly handled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to mock any English novel rudely.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Bronte's best-known book is a famous example of a novel.

clue.text: To prepare vintage, tread year's contents

indicators.note: contents says the letters are found inside the words just before it, spanning them

explanation.surface: To make wine from a vintage, tread the year's grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents' picks the letters from vintaGE TREAD Year's.
explanation.definitionFit: To get oneself set for something is to prepare, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Expelled school inspectorate, making one change

indicators.note: making one change says a single letter of the inspectorate's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Ofsted is the body that inspects schools in England

explanation.surface: A school inspectorate expelled someone and made one change.
explanation.walkthrough: OFSTED is the English schools inspectorate; 'making one change' swaps its F for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being removed or thrown out of a post is a synonym for expelled.

clue.text: Entices office workers? About time

indicators.note: About means going around, so the office workers enclose the letter for time

parts.note: temps are temporary office staff

explanation.surface: Office staff are lured in, with a question about time.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone with something attractive is to entice them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Picture army officer with old musical instrument

parts.note: pic is short for picture
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A picture shows an army officer holding an old instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The small high-pitched flute is a woodwind instrument, so an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: Young lady distributed medals

indicators.note: distributed suggests the letters are handed out and spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman hands out medals at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a young unmarried woman, as in a maiden in distress.

clue.text: Raw treat prepared for amphibious rodent

indicators.note: prepared hints at ingredients being worked into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncooked snack is made ready for a creature at home on land and in water.
explanation.definitionFit: The water vole, called by this name in Britain, is a rodent that lives on land and in rivers.

clue.text: Jewelled headdress: it elevated a painter

indicators.note: elevated means raised up, which in a down light turns the little word upside down

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A jewelled headdress lifted up a painter's status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns IT into TI in this down entry; RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jewelled crown worn by a princess is a decorative headdress.

clue.text: Wonderful going around foremost of night spots

indicators.note: going around says the slang for wonderful wraps around the letter

parts.note: ace is slang for wonderful

indicators.note: foremost of picks the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A wonderful time going round the best nightclub spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foremost of' takes N from night, and 'going around' puts ACE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin condition causing pimples is a matter of spots, a synonym by example.

clue.text: Garment sarts off small and rarely increases

indicators.note: a misprint of starts off, saying to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A garment begins small and seldom grows bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sarts off' is the clue's typing slip for 'starts off'; it takes the first letters of small, and, rarely, increases.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrapped dress worn by women in South Asia is a garment.

clue.text: Does walk, say, regularly, in Japanese city

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the words before it, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Female deer stroll steadily, as it were, around a city in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of DOES WALK SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The large port in Honshu is one of Japan's major cities.

clue.text: Minor quarrel to have in Cheltenham?

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A small row breaks out in the Gloucestershire town of Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham, in Gloucestershire, England, is famous for its mineral springs; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheltenham grew as a resort around medicinal springs, so it is an example of such a town.

clue.text: Music hall song, unspecific request to golf caddie?

definitions.meaning: a cockney music hall number made famous by Harry Champion
a golfer asking for whichever metal club comes to hand

explanation.surface: A golfer casually asks the caddie for a club, like an old music hall tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Music hall was British popular variety theatre; golf irons are metal-headed clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous old song shares its title with a casual ask for any metal golf club.
